mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Tuesday 4:07 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-10 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Designs the GPUs and networking gear that power most AI data centres.
items.why: Nvidia fell 5.4% on CPI day as reports about its China chip shipments and scrutiny of CEO Jensen Huang's ties to a former Megaspeed executive piled onto rate-hike worries; news reports put the stock about 30% below its early-October record. Posts say Wedbush's Dan Ives sketched a further 30% drop if Huang were to leave, which he framed as a scenario, not a forecast. Earnings are due Nov 17.

items.name: CoreWeave Inc
items.about: Rents out GPU cloud capacity for training and running AI models.
items.why: CoreWeave reported Q3 after Tuesday's close against consensus of about $3.5B revenue, with heavy interest costs (guided $860–940M) the main worry after the stock fell more than 40%. Posts quoting the release say revenue rose more than $1B from the prior quarter and the company expects about $9B in customer prepayments over the next three months; shares were up about 7% after hours at $52.57.

items.name: Netlist Inc
items.about: Makes memory modules and licenses memory patents, with long-running litigation against Samsung and Micron.
items.why: The crowd is waiting on Netlist's Q3 results, due after Tuesday's close; at the close the report had not yet appeared, and shares ended flat at $6.25. Posts say the stock gained about $0.73 over the prior two sessions and ask whether revenue from a Samsung arrangement will show up in the numbers; that claim is not confirmed.

items.name: Digital Turbine Inc
items.about: Sells app-distribution and mobile advertising software used by phone makers and carriers.
items.why: Digital Turbine fell 36.6% to $7.16 after its fiscal Q2 report on Nov 9, which had been pushed back a week to finalize the financials. Investing.com said revenue beat but management only reiterated its full-year EBITDA range, which disappointed after the earlier delay and an August restatement of Q1 results.

items.name: Senseonics Holdings Inc
items.about: Makes Eversense, an implantable continuous glucose monitor for people with diabetes.
items.why: Senseonics jumped as much as about 42% (to $13.95) after better-than-expected Q3 results, a higher 2026 sales outlook and a Raymond James upgrade, then gave almost all of it back to close up 2.8% at $10.07. Posts say the fade came from heavy selling into the spike and worries about a share offering; that is not confirmed.

items.name: Charter Communications Inc
items.about: Runs Spectrum, a major US cable broadband, TV and mobile provider.
items.why: Charter rose 10.6% to $133.99, recovering from an early low of $117.71, but a news search found no company-specific catalyst. Posts say short interest is around 15–16% of the float and describe the move as a short squeeze; that is crowd talk, not confirmed news.

items.name: Rocket Lab USA Inc
items.about: Launches small rockets, is building the larger Neutron rocket and makes spacecraft parts.
items.why: Rocket Lab climbed 6.2% to $62.49 after reporting Q3 on Nov 9. Posts citing the results say revenue grew about 73%, the backlog hit a record $3.57B and Neutron won more than $515M in new launch contracts before its first flight. The pending Iridium acquisition is still expected to close in 2027.

items.name: Venture Global Inc
items.about: Builds and runs liquefied natural gas export terminals in Louisiana.
items.why: Venture Global edged up 1.5% to $11.98 on heavy volume of about 16.6M shares, but no confirmed news was found. Posts speculate about a possible data-center power deal, a Qatar agreement, details of a BP settlement and FERC approval for higher output; all of that is unconfirmed.

items.name: ImmunityBio Inc
items.about: Develops immunotherapies; sells Anktiva for a form of bladder cancer.
items.why: ImmunityBio slipped 5% to $6.76. Posts say quarterly Anktiva sales fell short of hopes and complain about dilution, noting the share count is near 1 billion; those claims were not confirmed by a news search.

items.name: Rigetti Computing Inc
items.about: Builds superconducting quantum computers and sells access to them through the cloud.
items.why: Rigetti fell 6.5% to $12.13 heading into its Q3 report and slid another 9% or so after hours to about $11.84. Posts focus on how much revenue comes from system sales versus government grants; no confirmed details of the results were found.

items.name: Sanmina Corp
items.about: Contract manufacturer that builds electronics, including AI server racks through its ZT Systems unit.
items.why: Sanmina surged about 20% after hours on Nov 9 on its fiscal Q4 results, then gave back most of it on CPI day to close up 3.7% at $155.18. Posts citing the release say revenue rose 84% to $3.86B against about $3.48B expected, and fiscal 2027 guidance of $17.5–19.5B includes $7.5–9.0B from Cloud & AI Systems.

items.name: GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF
items.about: Leveraged ETF that aims to return twice Nvidia's daily move.
items.why: NVDL fell 10.8% to $19.30, double Nvidia's 5.4% drop on China-shipment reports and scrutiny of its CEO. Posts are mostly traders buying the dip ahead of Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings.

items.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc
items.about: Building a satellite network that connects directly to ordinary smartphones.
items.why: AST SpaceMobile fell 8.7% to $33.68 after its Q3 report. Investing.com reported that UBS cut its target to $43 from $78 over scaling delays, and posts say BofA cut to $45 from $80. Analysts flagged launch cadence and the extra cost of the company's new plan to build its own heavy-lift rocket.

items.name: Legend Biotech
items.about: Biotech that co-markets Carvykti, a CAR-T cell therapy for multiple myeloma, with Johnson & Johnson.
items.why: Legend fell 14.4% to $20.79, which Stocktwits News called on track for its worst day ever. Q3 revenue of $359.5M was up 32% and roughly in line, but investors focused on slowing US demand for Carvykti. Posts note the company is now profitable, with about $853M in cash, and still targets more than $5B in peak sales.

items.name: Hims & Hers Health Inc
items.about: Online telehealth platform selling prescription treatments for weight loss, hair loss, sexual health and more.
items.why: Hims & Hers dropped 17% to $19.03 after Q3 results posted Nov 9 missed on the bottom line and the company cut its revenue and 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook, according to Investing.com and StockTitan. Posts point to heavy put buying and rising short interest.

items.name: Firefly Aerospace Inc.
items.about: Builds small launch rockets and the Blue Ghost lunar lander.
items.why: Firefly slipped 2.4% to $23.73 ahead of its Q3 report after Tuesday's close and was down about 3% after hours. Posts compare it with Rocket Lab's post-earnings jump and focus on guidance.

items.name: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.
items.about: Video game publisher behind Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K and Zynga mobile games.
items.why: Take-Two jumped 8.3% to $224.66 even though its Nov 9 quarter missed: net bookings fell 18% to $1.60B. The company said GTA VI preorders are far exceeding expectations ahead of the Nov 19 launch and raised its full-year revenue guide to $7.98–8.18B. Piper Sandler sees a path to $290 next year.

items.name: Amprius Technologies Inc
items.about: Makes high-energy silicon-anode lithium-ion batteries for drones and aviation.
items.why: Amprius closed down 3.9% at $9.15 and fell about 14% after hours to $8.22 once Q3 results came out. Posts quoting the release say revenue rose 83% to $39.1M and the 2026 revenue outlook was raised to $145M; the call is Nov 11 at 8:30 am ET.

items.name: Luckin Coffee Inc - ADR
items.about: China's largest coffee chain by store count; its ADRs trade over the counter in the US.
items.why: Luckin rose 5.7% to $36.80, closing at the day's high, but a news search found no specific catalyst. Posts are mostly long-term holders celebrating and pointing to its store count closing in on Starbucks.

items.name: Trade Desk Inc
items.about: Runs a self-service platform that ad buyers use to purchase digital ads across the open internet.
items.why: Trade Desk was on Investing.com's after-hours movers list with its Q3 report on Nov 9. It dipped to $13.88 early Tuesday before rallying to close up 3.1% at $15.39 on about 55M shares. Posts argue over a bearish Citi stance; that detail is not confirmed.
